issues.legal_issue: An appellate factual finding cannot stand when it results from overlooking material evidence, misreading the record, or applying an unreasonable approach to the evidence.
material_facts: The High Court rejected the finding that the goods had been placed in the defendants’ custody after discounting witness testimony on grounds the Supreme Court found untenable.
The High Court overlooked relevant testimony and admissions, misread parts of the evidence, and made an error of record.
The Supreme Court found the plaintiff’s evidence more credible and weighty than the defendants’ evidence.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s finding on the custody of the goods was unsustainable and was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: A factual finding based on non-consideration of material evidence, misreading of evidence, errors of record, or a manifestly unreasonable approach cannot be sustained on appeal. No earlier case or statutory provision is relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: civil_appeal_reviewing_fact_finding and material_evidence_overlooked and (evidence_misread or record_error or unreasonable_evidentiary_approach)

predicates.civil_appeal_reviewing_fact_finding: The proceeding is an appeal in which a court reviews a factual finding made by a lower court.
predicates.material_evidence_overlooked: The lower court failed to consider evidence material to the factual finding.
predicates.evidence_misread: The lower court misunderstood or inaccurately read evidence relevant to its finding.
predicates.record_error: The lower court relied on a factual description contradicted by the record.
predicates.unreasonable_evidentiary_approach: The lower court assessed the evidence on grounds that were manifestly unreasonable.

issues.definition: When an appellate court is reviewing a factual finding and material evidence was overlooked alongside misread evidence, a record error, or an unreasonable evidentiary approach, the unsupported finding is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A person shown to have custody of goods entrusted for sale must account for the goods or their sale proceeds when the proceeds remain unpaid.
material_facts: The plaintiff’s goods were deposited in the defendants’ shop or godown and placed in their custody.
The defendants sold the goods, including the 21 bales at issue, and the sale proceeds were not paid to the plaintiff.
Witness testimony, purchasers’ evidence, business records, and an admission attributed to a defendant supported the plaintiff’s account.
The defendants offered no adequate explanation for the 21 bales or their proceeds.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff proved the claim for the unpaid proceeds of the 21 bales, and the defendants were liable for that claim.
issues.legal_principle: Once the plaintiff proved that the defendants possessed the goods, it was their duty to account for them. The Court assessed the oral and documentary evidence and the defendant’s admission; it relied on no statutory provision or earlier case for this principle.

rule.if: civil_goods_sale_claim and goods_entrusted_to_defendant and defendants_sold_goods and sale_proceeds_unpaid

predicates.civil_goods_sale_claim: The proceeding is a civil claim seeking payment for goods entrusted to another for sale.
predicates.goods_entrusted_to_defendant: The claimant placed the goods in the defendant’s custody for sale.
predicates.defendants_sold_goods: The defendant sold the goods entrusted to it.
predicates.sale_proceeds_unpaid: The defendant did not pay the claimant the proceeds of the sale.

issues.definition: In a civil claim for sale proceeds, when goods were entrusted to the defendant, the defendant sold them, and the proceeds remain unpaid, the defendant is liable to account for those proceeds.

issues.legal_issue: A court may permit late production of documents for good cause when the opposing party has an opportunity to address them and their admission causes no prejudice.
material_facts: The plaintiff filed documents with particulars supplied at the defendants’ request and under the trial court’s directions.
The trial court condoned the delay and directed the defendants to admit or deny the documents before evidence began.
The defendants complied and had an opportunity to rebut the documents.
The Supreme Court found no surprise or prejudice from their production.
issues.conclusion: The trial court did not err in permitting the documents to be produced, and the High Court was wrong to treat their admission as improper.
issues.legal_principle: Order 13, Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits the court to receive documents not produced at the required stage if good cause is shown to the court’s satisfaction. The provision’s purpose is to prevent belated production from working injustice; it requires no ritualistic form of order. No earlier case is relied on.

rule.if: civil_proceeding_with_late_documents and good_cause_for_late_filing and opposing_party_had_opportunity_to_respond and no_prejudice_from_admission

predicates.civil_proceeding_with_late_documents: The proceeding is a civil case in which a party seeks to produce documents after the usual stage for production.
predicates.good_cause_for_late_filing: The party gives a satisfactory reason for not producing the documents at the required stage.
predicates.opposing_party_had_opportunity_to_respon: The opposing party had a chance to admit or deny the documents and to present rebuttal evidence.
predicates.no_prejudice_from_admission: The timing and admission of the documents did not take the opposing party by surprise or impair its ability to contest them.

issues.definition: Late documents may be received in a civil proceeding when the party shows good cause, the opposing party can respond, and admission causes no prejudice.

issues.legal_issue: A claim should not be rejected for a supposed gap between pleadings and proof when the pleadings state the essential case and later particulars clarify it without changing that case.
material_facts: The plaint alleged that the defendants kept the plaintiff’s goods, sold them, and failed to pay the proceeds for 21 bales.
At the defendants’ request, the plaintiff supplied particulars under the trial court’s direction.
The plaintiff’s evidence sought to prove the case pleaded and clarified in those particulars.
The Supreme Court found no substantial variation between the pleadings and the evidence.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was wrong to find a wide gap between the plaintiff’s pleadings and proof.
issues.legal_principle: Pleadings are often loosely drafted and should not be scrutinised with such meticulous care that genuine claims are defeated on trivial grounds. Order 6, Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure was relevant to the court-directed provision of particulars. No earlier case is relied on.

rule.if: civil_claim_with_pleading_dispute and essential_case_stated_in_pleadings and later_particulars_clarify_claim and evidence_supports_pleaded_case

predicates.civil_claim_with_pleading_dispute: The proceeding is a civil claim in which a court considers whether the evidence departs from the pleadings.
predicates.essential_case_stated_in_pleadings: The pleadings set out the essential factual basis of the claim.
predicates.later_particulars_clarify_claim: Later particulars supply details of the pleaded case rather than introduce a materially different case.
predicates.evidence_supports_pleaded_case: The evidence supports the case stated in the pleadings as clarified by the particulars.

issues.definition: A civil claim is not rejected for a pleading-evidence variance when the pleadings state its essential basis, later particulars clarify it, and the evidence supports that case.

issues.legal_issue: A claim for proceeds from retail goods fails when reliable evidence does not establish their delivery and sale and the material account of the sale is absent from the pleadings.
material_facts: The plaintiff claimed the price of retail cloth allegedly sent for sale and relied in part on an account entry and a document that was unsigned and contained an unexplained discrepancy in its total.
The defendants denied receiving the goods, and the plaintiff did not reliably prove that the goods were delivered to or sold by the defendants or the alleged retailer.
The plaint and later particulars did not allege that the goods had been sold by the retailer identified in the plaintiff’s evidence.
The alleged retailer denied selling the plaintiff’s goods, and the plaintiff did not establish a contrary entry in that retailer’s account books.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff did not prove the retail-sale claim, and that claim was disallowed.
issues.legal_principle: A claimant must establish the factual basis of a pleaded claim with reliable evidence. An unsupported account entry and an unreliable document do not establish delivery and sale, particularly where the material account of the sale is not pleaded. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.civil_retail_sale_proceeds_claim: The proceeding is a civil claim for proceeds from goods allegedly sent for retail sale.
predicates.delivery_or_sale_not_reliably_proved: Reliable evidence does not establish that the goods were delivered for sale or were sold as alleged.
predicates.material_sale_account_absent_from_pleadi: The pleadings omit a material account of who sold the goods or how the sale occurred.

issues.definition: A civil claim for retail-sale proceeds is rejected when reliable evidence does not prove delivery or sale and the material sale account is absent from the pleadings.

issues.legal_issue: A claim for alleged cash loans fails when the claimant produces no supporting evidence.
material_facts: The plaintiff claimed an amount allegedly borrowed in cash by the defendants.
The plaintiff produced no evidence supporting that claim and did not seriously press it on appeal.
issues.conclusion: The claim for cash borrowings was properly disallowed.
issues.legal_principle: A claimant must prove a monetary claim with evidence; an unsupported allegation of cash borrowing does not establish liability. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on.

predicates.civil_cash_loan_claim: The proceeding is a civil claim seeking repayment of money allegedly lent in cash.
predicates.no_supporting_evidence_for_loan: The claimant provides no evidence supporting the alleged cash loan.

issues.definition: A civil claim for repayment of an alleged cash loan is rejected when the claimant provides no supporting evidence.

issues.legal_issue: An admitted payment must be credited against the proven principal before interest is calculated, and an excessive claimed interest rate may be reduced.
material_facts: The plaintiff proved a claim for the unpaid proceeds of the 21 bales.
The defendants had paid the plaintiff an amount that the plaintiff admitted receiving and credited against his overall claim.
The plaintiff’s method of crediting that payment did not first subtract it from the proven claim before calculating interest.
The Court considered the claimed interest rate too high and awarded interest at a lower rate.
issues.conclusion: The admitted payment was deducted from the proven principal before interest was calculated, and interest was allowed at a reduced rate.
issues.legal_principle: The Court required the admitted payment to be credited against the proven claim before interest was added and reduced the claimed rate as excessive. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this assessment.

rule.if: civil_money_recovery_claim and proven_principal and admitted_payment and claimed_interest_excessive

predicates.civil_money_recovery_claim: The proceeding is a civil claim seeking recovery of money and interest.
predicates.proven_principal: The claimant establishes a principal amount recoverable from the defendant.
predicates.admitted_payment: The claimant admits receiving a payment from the defendant that must be credited against the claim.
predicates.claimed_interest_excessive: The court finds the interest rate claimed to be too high.

issues.definition: In a civil money-recovery claim, when principal is proved, a payment is admitted, and the claimed interest is excessive, the payment is credited before interest and the interest rate is reduced.
